design_intent.purpose: Behavior is defined by the YAML rules.

yaml_ports.name: enq_req
yaml_ports.description: Packed request_t enqueue payload; validity is carried only by req_valid

yaml_ports.name: enq_ready
yaml_ports.description: High when any queue slot is free

yaml_ports.name: req_array
yaml_ports.description: DEPTH-entry request_t array, DEPTH defaults to 4

rules: request_t does not contain a valid field; req_valid is the only validity source
enq_ready is high when any req_valid entry is 0, or when deq_en will free sel_idx in the same cycle
enqueue inserts into the lowest-index free slot; if the queue is full and deq_en is asserted, enqueue inserts at sel_idx
if enqueue and dequeue target the same index in one clock cycle, enqueue wins and the new request remains valid
suppress dequeue when reuse_slot is true: use if (deq_en && !reuse_slot)
deq_en clears req_valid[sel_idx] only when no same-index enqueue wins

invariants: req_valid is the sole validity source
enq_ready == OR of free slots, plus same-cycle deq slot reuse
first free slot receives enq_req; full queue plus deq_en inserts at sel_idx
same-cycle enqueue to a dequeued slot leaves req_valid set and stores the new payload

implementation_required: use request_t for enq_req and req_array entries

do not drop a request unless deq_en clears its selected slot
update entry data and req_valid with explicit next-state ordering so same-index enqueue/dequeue is deterministic
generated RTL must include an explicit reuse_slot signal; do not rely on assignment ordering between deq and enq writes
